FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard [ P : 58 ] ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after 
the draft finalized by the Methods of Test for Petroleum, Petroleum Products and Lubricants Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 

In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, 
observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for 
rounding off numerical values ( revised )\ 



IS 1448 [ P : 58 ] : 1991 



Indian Standard 

METHODS OF TEST FOR PETROLEUM 
AND ITS PRODUCTS 

[ P : 58 ] 
DETERMINATION OF INSOLUBLES IN GREASES 

( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 The method prescribed is intended for the 
determination of insoluble? in conventional 
greases which consist essentially of mineral oil 
and soap. The method is not applicable to 
greases containing non-soap thicketiers which are 
not broken by dilute mineral acids. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 



IS No. 

265 : 1987 

323 : 1959 

1745 : 1978 



Title 



Hydrochloric acid ( third revision ) 
Rectified spirit 

Petroleum hydrocarbon solvent 
( second revision ) 

3 SIGNIFICANCE AND USE 

3.1 The method can be used to determine the 
insoluble content ( graphite, molybdenum disulp- 
bide etc ) of lubricating greases. The method is 
applicable to conventional soap base lubricating 
greases. 

4 REAGENTS 

4.1 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid 

approximately 10 percent by mass of absolute 
hydrochloric acid ( see IS 265 : 1987 ). 

4.2 Petroleum Hydrocarbon Solvent ( 60/80 ) 

(see IS 1745: 1978). 



4.3 Rectified Spirit 

95 percent by volume ( see IS 323 : 1959 ). 

5 PROCEDURE 

5.1 Weigh into a conical flask a suitable quantity 
( 8 to 30 g ) of the material, accurately to the 
nearest 0*1 g, spread the grease sample uniformly 
on the sides of the flask for better dispersion and 
decomposition. Add 50 ml of petroleum hydro- 
carbon solvent. Add 50 ml of dilute hydochloric 
acid. Fit up the conical flask to a reflux con- 
denser and reflux until all soap has decomposed 
and the upper petroleum hydrocarbon solvent 
layer is clear. Filter the undissolved matter 
through a tared Gooch crucible provided with a 
suitable mat. Wash the conical flask and the 
crucible with warm ( 60 to 63°G ) water and 
petroleum hydrocarbon solvent and finally wash 
the crucible with rectified spirit. Dry the crucible 
contents at 120°G and weigh to a constant weight* 
Cool in a desiccator and weigh. 

6 CALCULATIONS AND REPORTING 

6.1 Calculate the percentage of insolubles as: 

100 X a 



Insolubles, percent = 



w 



where 

a — weight of the insolubles, and 
w = weight of the sample taken.

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been 
produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of 
inspection, tosting and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated 
by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for con- 
formity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence 
for the use oft he Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be 
obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country.
